summary: Malawi combines forest and land-use measures across restoration, conservation and agriculture. Its forestry package covers up to 2 million ha, with 534,478 ha identified for additional forestry activities over the coming decade. Restoration targets 4.5 million ha of afforestation, reforestation and assisted natural regeneration by 2035—equal to 182% of the 2.47 million ha mapped as forest in 2022—plus 100,000 ha of wetland restoration, 36,000 ha of riparian planting and a rise from 36% in 2025 to 50% by 2063 in afforestation/reforestation. Conservation sets 2.4 million ha of forest protection by 2035 (97% of current forest), 300,000 ha under sustainable forest and landscape management, 60% wetland protection by 2035, 80% fisheries co-management and 25,000 ha of nature-based solutions by 2035. Agriculture targets 240,000 ha of conservation agriculture by 2030, 100,000 ha under agroforestry and 1 million ha for drought- and early-maturing crop varieties. Agriculture covers 53.1% of Malawi.
